circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281-kilometre track designed by Hermann Tilke on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island, has served as the venue for Formula One's season-closing Abu Dhabi Grand Prix since 2009. It became the second Middle Eastern Formula One circuit after Bahrain, followed later by venues in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the Formula One Australian Grand Prix each year alongside various support categories and racing events. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: The 4. 326 km track located in Spielberg, Austria originally operated as the Österreichring and held the Austrian Grand Prix annually between 1970 and 1987. Following extensive modifications and a reduction in length, the circuit was renamed and returned to Formula One racing, hosting the Grand Prix once more from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street-based racing venue in Azerbaijan's capital city, positioned along the Baku Boulevard waterfront. At 6. 003 kilometers, it ranks as the fourth-lengthiest track on the F1 calendar.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that hosted the inaugural Formula One race in the Middle East that same year, alongside accommodating various motorsport categories including GP2 Series and drag racing. The FIA Grade 1 licensed facility has featured multiple track configurations and previously hosted the Desert 400 with Australian V8 Supercars from 2006 to 2010, along with 24-hour endurance competitions.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya in Montmeló spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced combination of extended straights and diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for all-round racing performance. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: This 7-kilometer Belgian circuit near Stavelot has been hosting Formula One racing since 1950, making it one of the championship's oldest venues. The track has continuously held the Belgian Grand Prix annually since 1985, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, this 4. 361 km circuit serves as the home of the Canadian Grand Prix in Formula One racing. Beyond its primary role in F1, the venue has accommodated various international motorsporting series including sports car championships and North American racing competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, the Shanghai International Circuit hosts the Chinese Grand Prix, which returned to the calendar in 2024 after a five-year absence from 2020 to 2023, having previously run from 2004 to 2019. The venue also accommodates other motorsport events, including an electric racing series that began in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near villages in Northamptonshire, England, Silverstone Circuit has been the primary venue for the British Grand Prix since 1948 and notably hosted the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. After alternating between three circuits from the mid-1950s through the 1980s, the British Grand Prix became a permanent fixture at Silverstone from 1987 onwards, which also stages a MotoGP round.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, a 4. 381 km circuit located near Budapest in Hungary, has hosted the Hungarian Grand Prix since 1986, making it the first Formula One venue in a communist country. Built in just eight months, faster than any other F1 circuit, the track was constructed outside the city near a major highway after plans for a street circuit in Budapest's central park were rejected by the government.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, the Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km track constructed in 1922 as Europe's oldest permanent racing facility and the world's third purpose-built circuit. The venue has continuously hosted the Italian Grand Prix since 1949, except during 1980 renovations, and earned its "Temple of Speed" nickname through its distinctive design featuring extended straights and fast corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: The Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport venue situated in Mie Prefecture and operated by Honda Mobilityland. With a capacity of 155,000 spectators, it has become synonymous with hosting major Formula One races and serves as a premier destination for international motorsport competition.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street track in Paradise, Nevada that snakes through the famous Las Vegas Boulevard district, featuring iconic venues such as the MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas. The layout incorporates the heart of the city's casino and hotel corridor, creating a unique urban racing environment. Formula One has utilized this configuration for its Las Vegas Grand Prix events.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit named in honor of brothers Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, both fatal racing casualties in the 1960s and 1970s. The venue has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix across three separate eras, returning to the championship in 2015 on its current layout after a 23-year absence, with the event rebranded as the Mexico City Grand Prix from 2021 onwards.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary track constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, Florida, stretching 3. 363 miles with 19 corners and an average qualifying speed of approximately 139 mph. Designed by specialist circuit architects Apex Circuit Design, the venue was created specifically to host the Miami Grand Prix, which joined the Formula One calendar beginning in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street course that winds through the urban streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine, encircling the harbour in Monaco's principality. Though situated primarily within the Monte Carlo district, the track is frequently known by that neighbourhood's name both colloquially and in official contexts.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes west of Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that made its Formula One comeback in 2021 hosting the revived Dutch Grand Prix. The partnership between the circuit and Formula One will conclude after the 2026 season.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: Situated north of Doha in Qatar, Lusail International Circuit is a 5. 419-kilometre track featuring a 1. 068-kilometre main straight and holding FIA Grade 1 status.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian racing facility in São Paulo that opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace following his fatal 1977 aviation accident. The counterclockwise circuit features a kart track dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street track positioned along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront, serving as the venue for the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix beginning in 2021 and more recently hosting Formula E racing from 2025 onward.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's downtown waterfront district, utilizing public roads around the Marina Bay area to create a temporary racing venue that incorporates multiple planning zones.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km Spanish circuit is renowned for its balanced design combining extended straight sections with diverse corner configurations, making it suitable for testing all aspects of vehicle performance. The track holds FIA Grade 1 certification and features grandstands accommodating approximately 140,700 spectators.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 facility that serves as the permanent home of Formula One's United States Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the track hosts multiple racing series including MotoGP's Motorcycle Grand Prix of the Americas and endurance racing events, while previously welcoming various other motorsport championships.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a racing driver of Thai and British heritage who represents Thailand in Formula One, currently driving for Williams.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has secured two World Drivers' Championships with Renault in 2005 and 2006 and claimed 32 Grand Prix victories across 23 seasons. Beyond single-seater racing, Alonso has achieved notable success in endurance competition, winning the 2018-19 FIA World Endurance Championship and multiple prestigious events including two Le Mans 24-hour races and the 2019 Daytona 24-hour race, making him the sole driver to win both the Formula One and World Endurance championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli joined Mercedes' Formula One lineup in 2025 and has already achieved six race victories in his early career.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races in Formula One as a member of the Audi team. The former junior formula competitor has progressed to the sport's premier championship level.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas, now competing for Cadillac in Formula One, has achieved two runner-up finishes in the World Drivers' Championship during his time with Mercedes in 2019 and 2020. Over his 13-year career in the sport, he has secured victories in 10 Grand Prix races.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine motorsport competitor currently racing in Formula One with the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan combines endurance racing commitments in the LMP2 category with a Formula One reserve role at Haas, having made seven Grand Prix starts during the 2024-2025 seasons.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The 2020 Italian Grand Prix at Monza marked a career highlight when he secured victory while driving for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar is a French-Algerian racing driver who represents France in Formula One while driving for Red Bull Racing.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari, holding joint-record status with seven world championship titles alongside Michael Schumacher. He leads the sport in multiple statistical categories, including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in Formula One history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races in Formula One for Audi, bringing significant experience from his extensive career in the sport. Beyond single-seaters, he achieved notable success in endurance racing, securing victory at the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while competing for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand-born racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a driver from Monaco, currently races for Ferrari in Formula One. He finished second in the 2022 drivers' championship and has accumulated nine Grand Prix victories throughout his career spanning nine seasons.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Danish driver Kevin Magnussen competed in Formula One across two separate periods, from 2014-2020 and again from 2022-2024. Currently, he races for BMW in the FIA World Endurance Championship with WRT while also pursuing a part-time NASCAR career with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British Formula One driver, secured the 2025 World Drivers' Championship while racing for McLaren. Throughout his eight seasons in the sport, he has claimed victory in 12 Grand Prix events.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. The 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix victory with Alpine stands as a notable achievement in his racing career.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez competes in Formula One for Cadillac, bringing extensive experience from his 15 seasons in the sport. He achieved his highest championship finish as runner-up in 2023 while with Red Bull and has secured six race victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri is an Australian driver competing in Formula One for McLaren, where he has secured nine Grand Prix victories over his four seasons in the championship.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known by the nickname "the Honey Badger", competed in Formula One spanning 14 seasons from 2011 until 2024, during which he secured eight Grand Prix victories.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has secured seven Grand Prix victories throughout his eight seasons in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes for Williams in Formula One, having accumulated four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who raced in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to endurance racing. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, having previously driven in IMSA's LMP2 class for Era Motorsport.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin. He represents his nation in the sport's top racing category.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda is a Japanese driver who has competed in Formula One across multiple seasons from 2021 through 2025, currently functioning as a reserve driver for Red Bull Racing and its sister team Racing Bulls.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: A Dutch and Belgian racing driver competing for Red Bull Racing, Verstappen has secured four consecutive Formula One World Drivers' Championship titles between 2021 and 2024. Across his 12-season career, he has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu, the sole Chinese driver to participate in Formula One, competed in the sport from 2022 to 2024 and currently holds a reserve position with Cadillac.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has competed under the Alpine banner since 2021, following its rebranding from Renault F1 Team as a factory operation for the French automotive group's sports car division. Alpine's sole victory came through Esteban Ocon at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix, with the team currently powered by Mercedes engines and representing France in the championship.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has a multi-faceted presence in Formula One history through different organizational structures, with the contemporary incarnation operating as a works team alongside title sponsor Aramco.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker Ferrari, is Formula One's longest-established and most accomplished team, participating continuously in the World Championship since its inception in 1950. The squad, famously nicknamed "the Prancing Horse" after its emblematic symbol, holds an unmatched record of uninterrupted competition across the sport's entire modern history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas founded this American-licensed Formula One outfit in 2014, with the team competing from 2016 onward. Leadership transitioned in early 2024 when Ayao Komatsu assumed the principal role, succeeding the founding team principal who had guided the organization since its inception.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss engineering and racing outfit established in 1970, Sauber competed in Formula One from 1993 until 2025 as one of sport's longest-serving constructors. The team achieved notable success in endurance racing, including victory at the 1989 Le Mans 24 Hours with Mercedes-Benz, before being acquired by Audi in 2024 to serve as the foundation for Audi's entry into Formula One.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren is a British Formula One outfit headquartered at its Technology Centre in Woking that competes under Mastercard sponsorship. The team operates as part of the McLaren Group, with ultimate ownership held by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: The Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One Team, based in Brackley and operating under a German licence, represents Mercedes-Benz's continuous involvement in Formula One since 1954 as both constructor and engine supplier. From January 2022, ownership became equally shared among Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff. The team carries the historic "Silver Arrows" designation, synonymous with Mercedes' racing heritage.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that commenced competition in 2024, operating as one of two teams under Red Bull GmbH's ownership alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with additional facilities near its sister team in Milton Keynes, the squad represents the conglomerate's second competitive entry in the sport.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian-based Formula One team that entered the sport in 2024 as part of Red Bull GmbH's two-team ownership structure. Operating from Faenza with a secondary facility near its sister team Red Bull Racing in Milton Keynes, the squad functions as Red Bull's second constructor in the championship.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: An Austrian-licensed Formula One team headquartered in England, Red Bull Racing has been a fixture in the sport since its 2005 establishment, operating as one of two racing programs under Red Bull GmbH's ownership. The team was led by Christian Horner throughout its first two decades before Laurent Mekies assumed the role of team principal in 2025.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams is a British Formula One team and constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding an earlier unsuccessful racing operation. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team will compete in 2026 as Atlassian Williams F1 Team.
